text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Coalition Party is to form a minority government with the rural parties union and the Centre Party was left outside the coalition.
- The privatisation agency decided to sell chemical plant Kiviter to company Infravest for 63 million kroons and 230 million kroon investments over three years.
- The central election commission has received reports on parties' campaign costs. The Reform party leads the list with 2 million kroons.
- The first link of the waste water treatment plant in Tartu was opened. The project was made possible by a loan from the EBRD and aid from Switzerland.
- Estonia does not intend to recognise Chechen independence nor allow the opening of an embassy, foreign ministry officials say.
- Tiit Vaehi met President Lennart Meri at midnight and proposed ambassador to the U.S. Toomas Hendrik Ilves for foreign minister.

- The U.S. Ambassador to Sweden did not link NATO membership for Estonia and Latvia with the situation of the Russian population in these countries, the U.S. Embassy in Sweden announced, contradicting news reports.
- Oil firm Pakterminal headed the list of the 100 most succesful companies in Estonia, the Chamber of Industry and Commerce and Aripaev announced yesterday.
